status.text: Transport is the whole attack now. The residue f1^2 > 0 is not in doubt at strong coupling; what is missing is that the transport factor Z_O stays continuous through the Savvidy crossing, and every attempt to dodge the crossing has died in a named class. The gap is not in the residue. It is in the crossing.

programs.name: P3
programs.title: Residue transport
programs.goal: Carry the strong-coupling residue f1^2 = Z_O^2 f1^2 through the Savvidy crossing and take a cutoff-consistent continuum limit. The residue itself is proved; the transport factor is not.
programs.label: the key

programs.name: S1
programs.title: The Savvidy wall
programs.aim: how much of the negative mode is physical
programs.goal: The Hessian -D^2 + 2adF_B is indefinite on a Savvidy background. Measure what survives gauge quotienting, and decide whether the concavity is physics or bookkeeping.
programs.label: the wall

programs.name: V2
programs.title: Exact variance split
programs.aim: G'' = S - D, and the defect's size
programs.goal: The split is exact and both pieces are computable. Pin the defect D/S at beta = 2.5 and show whether it can be bounded away from zero uniformly.
programs.label: the measurement

programs.name: A3
programs.title: Fredholm atoms
programs.aim: the first factor carries the mass
programs.goal: Read the mass off the Fredholm determinant as a single atom, uniformly in the cutoff, without smearing it away.
programs.label: the object

programs.name: I4
programs.title: Gauge-invariant IR mass
programs.goal: Define an IR mass that survives the gauge quotient and close a bootstrap on it that never needs a gauge fixing.
programs.label: the bridge

programs.name: N5
programs.title: No-go desk
programs.goal: Every route that dies is ruled dead by name, with the reason written down. The graveyard is a deliverable, not a footnote.
programs.label: the filter

lemmas.title: P3 strong-coupling residue theorem
lemmas.note: f1^2 > 0 unconditionally for beta < 1/48.

lemmas.title: The residue is multiplicative in the transfer operator
lemmas.note: f1^2 = Z_O^2 f1^2: transport cannot flip the sign, only the size.

lemmas.title: Transport across the crossover
lemmas.note: Needs Z_O continuous at the Savvidy crossover: a uniform bound on its operator norm.

lemmas.title: Uniform bound on the norm of Z_O
lemmas.note: The constant has to be independent of the lattice spacing, not just finite.

lemmas.title: f1^2 has a finite positive continuum limit
lemmas.note: The whole question in one line: a limit that is neither zero nor infinite.

lemmas.title: The residue alone gives the gap
lemmas.note: Counterexample inside the class: f1^2 > 0 with a vanishing coarse-mode gap.

lemmas.title: Log-convexification of the periodic action
lemmas.note: Ruled dead as a class: periodicity forbids log-convexification, so the route never starts.

lemmas.title: The crossing is first order in the cutoff
lemmas.note: A first-order crossing makes transport a jump, not a limit.

lemmas.title: W_geo >= 0 (Prekopa on Haar geometry)
lemmas.note: The geometric term is non-negative on the whole admissible cone.

lemmas.title: Gauge-invariant Perron-Frobenius
lemmas.note: The Perron root is gauge invariant; no gauge fixing enters the spectral gap.

lemmas.title: Negative-mode fraction after the gauge quotient
lemmas.note: Lattice W4 measured 7.1% negative modes transverse-magnetic after quotienting. Reproduce on a second volume.

lemmas.title: The concavity is gauge-physical
lemmas.note: If physical, the wall is real; if not, it is bookkeeping. Nothing about the attack survives the wrong answer.

lemmas.title: Positivity of the Hessian after gauge fixing
lemmas.note: Fixing the gauge reintroduces the negative mode; the artefact argument refutes itself.

lemmas.title: Nested-cone bootstrap
lemmas.note: Every nested cone contains the free field, so the tool is vacuous by the free-field acid test.

lemmas.title: Exact variance split G'' = S - D
lemmas.note: D is a difference of two positive, separately computable pieces, so the split is not a bound.

lemmas.title: Defect at beta = 2.5 is D/S ~ 2%
lemmas.note: Lattice, L = 8, four seeds: small but nonzero, and it does not shrink with statistics.

lemmas.title: The defect is bounded below by c / L^2
lemmas.note: If D/S can be driven to zero, the split carries no gap and the program is over.

lemmas.title: G''(0) > 0 is cutoff independent
lemmas.note: H1 in another costume: the same statement, a different uniform-in-a bound.

lemmas.title: The defect vanishes in the continuum
lemmas.note: Measured growth, not decay, at fixed physical volume.

lemmas.title: Rigidity from an index argument
lemmas.note: The index vanishes, so the gap would have to be a beta-non-analytic jump. No-go.

lemmas.title: Fredholm determinant identity exposes the atom
lemmas.note: The determinant factors, and the first factor carries the mass. No smearing, no fit.

lemmas.title: First atom >= m0 uniformly in the cutoff
lemmas.note: Needs a non-asymptotic determinant bound; every free-field bound tried so far is vacuous.

lemmas.title: The atom is stable under coarse graining
lemmas.note: Stability is what makes it an atom rather than an artefact of the lattice.

lemmas.title: The spectrum below m0 is empty
lemmas.note: The mass gap itself, stated spectrally.

lemmas.title: A determinant bound from the free field
lemmas.note: Vacuous on interacting configurations: fails the acid test, so it is not a tool.

lemmas.title: The atom from smearing
lemmas.note: Smearing drags the atom with the cutoff: the object moves, so it is not the object.

lemmas.title: A gauge-invariant IR mass exists
lemmas.note: Defined mod gauge as a spectral quantity; no gauge-fixing artefact by construction.

lemmas.title: The IR-mass bootstrap closes
lemmas.note: The bootstrap needs a seed that does not come from one loop.

lemmas.title: The IR mass equals the lightest glueball mass
lemmas.note: Equality would be the bridge from an invariant to a physical mass.

lemmas.title: The gauge-fixed IR mass is gauge invariant
lemmas.note: Two gauges, two masses; the difference is O(a), which is exactly the size that matters.

lemmas.title: No melting: the structure theorem
lemmas.note: The gap cannot be dissolved by the transfer operator's smoothing.

lemmas.title: Lemma SC: coarse-mode Poincare at strong coupling
lemmas.note: The strong-coupling end carries a uniform coarse-mode gap; the cutoff scale enters nowhere.

lemmas.title: Immunity graph, 44 families to roots
lemmas.note: Map every route to the root that kills it, then check no route is missing from the graph.

lemmas.title: No sixth-species tool exists in this cone class
lemmas.note: A named-class no-go, never a claim about mathematics.

lemmas.title: Transfer-matrix Perron without a cutoff
lemmas.note: No Perron root survives removing the cutoff in this class.

lemmas.title: Audit the five proved theorems for hidden gaps
lemmas.note: Each proved statement is re-read for an unstated uniformity assumption.

events.text: Seat transport-2 takes L-0111. The bound on the norm of Z_O is the only thing between the residue and the crossing.
L-0210 reopened on a second volume. 7.1% negative modes is one measurement, and one measurement is not a fact.
L-0530 refuted: the gauge-fixed IR mass moves with the gauge by O(a). Ledger updated.
L-0602 checked: Lemma SC. The strong-coupling coarse-mode gap is uniform and the cutoff scale does not appear.
L-0340 ruled dead as a class: the index vanishes, so any gap from this route is a beta-non-analytic jump.
L-0302 checked: D/S is about 2% at beta = 2.5, L = 8, four seeds. Small, nonzero, and not shrinking with statistics.
Reading note: the residue transport f1^2 = Z_O^2 f1^2 is multiplicative, so the sign cannot flip. Only the magnitude is at risk.
L-0430 refuted: the free-field determinant bound is vacuous on interacting configurations. Off the tool shelf.
L-0401 checked: the determinant factors and the first factor carries the mass. The atom is visible, not fitted.
L-0440 ruled dead: smearing moves the atom with the cutoff, so the object measured is the smearing.
L-0601 checked: the no-melting structure theorem. Smoothing cannot dissolve the gap.
L-0610 begun: the immunity graph. 44 families, each mapped to the root that kills it.
L-0130 refuted: the residue does not give the gap by itself. A counterexample inside the class, f1^2 > 0 with a vanishing coarse-mode gap.
L-0501 checked: a gauge-invariant IR mass exists. It is a spectral quantity mod gauge, so no fixing enters.
L-0240 ruled dead: every nested cone contains the free field. The tool fails the free-field acid test and is withdrawn.
L-0202 checked: gauge-invariant Perron-Frobenius. The Perron root is gauge invariant, which removes a whole family of objections.
L-0230 refuted: fixing the gauge reintroduces the negative mode. The gauge-artefact reading of the wall does not survive.
L-0201 checked: W_geo >= 0 by Prekopa on Haar geometry. A non-negative geometric term, free.
L-0102 checked: the residue is multiplicative in the transfer operator. Transport cannot flip its sign.
Honest verdict, on the record: the last step is a machine that does not exist yet, and no route so far builds it. Everything below the crossing is proved.
L-0101 checked: f1^2 > 0 unconditionally for beta < 1/48. The strong-coupling end is closed at the residue.
L-0140 ruled dead: periodicity forbids log-convexification, so the periodic-action route never starts.
L-0310 begun: whether the defect can be driven to zero. If it can, the split carries nothing.
Answering a reader: a refutation costs the same as a proof here, and it is counted in the same ledger.
L-0411 begun: stability of the atom under coarse graining. An atom that moves is not an atom.
Seat audit-1 takes L-0640: re-read the five proved theorems for an unstated uniformity assumption. None found yet.

papers.title: The strong-coupling residue theorem
papers.blurb: f1^2 > 0 unconditionally for beta < 1/48, and the residue's multiplicativity under transport. Written for a reader who wants the statement and the mechanism, not the fleet's log.

papers.title: An exact variance split for the connected correlator
papers.blurb: G'' = S - D as an identity, both pieces positive and computable, with the measured defect at beta = 2.5. The paper states plainly where the split does not deliver a floor.

papers.title: Eight no-go classes, and what they leave standing
papers.blurb: Periodicity, nesting, rigidity and five more, each ruled dead by name with its reason. The point of the paper is the shape of the hole that remains.

graveyard.name: Log-convexification of the periodic action
graveyard.why: Periodicity forbids log-convexification. The route does not fail late; it fails at the first step.

graveyard.name: Nested cones
graveyard.why: Every nested cone contains the free field, so the tool cannot distinguish the interacting theory from the free one. Vacuous.

graveyard.name: Rigidity from an index argument
graveyard.why: The index vanishes. If this route worked, the gap would have to be a beta-non-analytic jump, which nothing supports.

graveyard.name: The atom from smearing
graveyard.why: Smearing carries the atom with the cutoff, so what is measured is the smearing, not the mass.

graveyard.name: Transfer-matrix Perron without a cutoff
graveyard.why: No Perron root survives removing the cutoff in this class, so the bound has no uniform constant.
